# Client GameTest weights for -PclientShard=i/n (gradle/gametest.gradle.kts): `<simple class name> <seconds>`.
# Generated by tools/client_weights.py, never by hand. Seconds: the mean over CI runs 46059180670 and 46061730162 and 46067559615 and 46069831431 and 46070846273 and 46072024137 of the gap between a class's START line and the next one in each shard's client job log, the last class of a shard running to the job's final `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` line. Each run's times are scaled so its total over the classes every run ran equals the mean total (runner speed varied about 1.3x). Rounded, at least 1, the least the file accepts: a class at 1 starts and ends within a second.
# A name is simple, or fully qualified when two classes share a simple name (the full name wins). A class not listed counts as 10 s, and a name ending in Scenario as 1 s, so a new class needs no entry here and the shards still cover every
# class; an entry for a class that no longer exists is ignored. Stale numbers only unbalance the shards, never
# drop a test. Refresh from green client job logs when the shard wall times drift apart, with at least three runs, so one loaded runner does not skew a class.
# Merged (#1574) with the entries of the file this one replaces (#1554's five-shard run) for the classes the runs above did not reach: the tool's numbers win. The classes this change split (StaleClientLightClientTest into itself and StaleClientLightTrials{A,B,C}ClientTest, HandBreakClientTest and HandBreakIronClientTest, PodDriveSmoothClientTest and PodDriveSmoothDrivesClientTest) come only from these runs, so no class outweighs a shard (gradle/ci-budget.txt).
# Estimates, not from a run: BoreTripsClientTest runs 6 trips, not 10 (125 s measured for 10, 30 s of it start-up); PodDriveSmoothDrivesClientTest is the jittered drives that PodDriveSmoothClientTest ran before it was split (about 155 s whole, 113 s of it the first class); refresh both from the next runs.
